title: Telemonitoring data support postoperative complication prediction
summary: Regularized logistic regression combined clinical features, symptom reports and pedometer data to evaluate 30-day complications after cancer surgery. The proof-of-concept study used 52 patients from two pilots and reported an AUROC of 0.74 with nested patient-level cross-validation. Data segments at or after complications were excluded. Small, heterogeneous cohorts and uneven wearable data limit generalizability; clinical intervention benefit was not tested.
organization: City of Hope National Medical Center

source_review.scope: Primary full paper relevant model Methods, study Results and limitations; exact primary front-matter identity and Europe PMC metadata checked.

evidence.tested: Nested leave-one-patient-out evaluation of postoperative complications, preserving repeated observations within patient folds.
evidence.unknown: External replication, real-time deployment and benefit from earlier intervention remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Regularized supervised learning combines clinical, patient-reported and wearable predictors with patient-grouped tuning/evaluation.
